Article Title: Venezuela earthquake toll rises to 6,301; over 9,500 homes deemed high-risk
Article Text:
Venezuela quake toll rises to 6,301; over 9,500 homes deemed high-risk. (File Photo)

Over 53,000 homes assessed

Two quakes struck within a minute

More than six weeks after two powerful earthquakes struck Venezuela, the death toll has risen to 6,301, while more than 9,500 homes have been classified as high-risk, underscoring the scale of the country's prolonged recovery and reconstruction challenge.National Assembly President Jorge Rodriguez announced the latest figures on Monday in an update posted on his Telegram channel. Rodriguez, who also heads the command overseeing temporary camps, said 287 homes have so far been delivered to people affected by the June 24 earthquakes.Authorities have assessed 53,314 homes since the disaster, with 31,336 deemed habitable and 12,411 placed under restricted access because of damage. Another 9,567 homes were classified as high-risk.The death toll has continued to rise as rescue, debris-removal and recovery operations progress. On July 12, authorities had reported 4,490 deaths, 16,740 injuries and 17,907 people left homeless, indicating a sharp increase in the reported human toll in the weeks since the earthquakes.The disaster has also caused extensive economic damage. Direct physical losses have been estimated at $19.6 billion, with residential buildings accounting for 47% of the damage.Infrastructure represented another 27%, while non-residential buildings accounted for 26%.Reconstruction costs could eventually reach $50 billion, once rebuilding and structural improvements are included.Venezuela was hit by earthquakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude on June 24, with the two powerful shocks occurring about a minute apart in northern Venezuela, west of Caracas.The earthquakes caused widespread building damage, power outages and disruptions to public services. Schools were closed, with some converted into temporary shelters, while the country's main international airport was temporarily shut as authorities assessed the damage.With nearly 9,600 homes now classified as high-risk and only 287 replacement homes delivered, Venezuela faces a major housing and reconstruction challenge in the weeks and months ahead.
Article Summary: Death toll rises to 6,301; over 9,500 homes deemed high-risk. Over 53,000 homes assessed since two quakes struck within a minute on June 24. Direct physical losses estimated at $19.6 billion, with residential buildings accounting for 47% of the damage.

Article Title: Trump Media Q2 results: US president-led media venture posts $238 m loss as crypto holdings tumble
Article Text:
Crypto losses deepen Trump Media’s woes as company doubles down on Truth Social

Trump Media shifts focus back to social media

Truth API takes centre stage

Paid service draws scrutiny

Nuclear fusion venture to continue

Trump Media & Technology, the company behind US President Donald Trump's Truth Social platform, reported a $238 million loss in the second quarter, as the value of its bitcoin and Cronos holdings tumbled. The three-month loss through June was more than 10 times the loss recorded a year earlier. In per-share terms, the company's loss widened from 8 cents to 86 cents.The sharp deterioration came even as revenue more than doubled to $1.7 million from a year earlier, marking an 89% rise. Excluding unrealised paper losses on its crypto holdings, along with taxes, interest and other items, Trump Media's operating loss rose to $164 million from $44 million a year earlier.Trump Media ended June with more than $400 million in cash and short-term investments. It also held $1.2 billion in bitcoin and bitcoin-related assets.The company also said it was changing course after a year of expanding into businesses beyond media.New chief executive Kevin McGurn said on a conference call after the earnings release that initiatives including online betting and crypto would now largely be abandoned as the company returns its focus to social media.“We made the disciplined choice to pivot in order to invest more time and resources in our most important initiatives,” McGurn said. “We will say no to things or change course as warranted,” the executive told AP.Trump Media's stock, which had already fallen 8% during regular trading, slipped slightly in after-hours trading after the earnings report.McGurn is placing greater emphasis on Truth API, a new service that gives Wall Street trading firms early access to posts from leading users on Truth Social.The service includes access to posts from Trump, the platform's most-followed user, whose posts have often moved markets when he announces major US policy shifts on the site.Trump Media is charging $60,000 to $100,000 a month for Truth API and has already signed 10 customers, McGurn said. Most are high-frequency trading firms that buy and sell in milliseconds.“We’re in the early innings,” McGurn said, adding that the potential market extends beyond traders to data centre companies, news organisations and developers of large language models.With 10 customers, the service could generate between $7 million and $12 million a year, or roughly two to three times the company's entire revenue last year.The service has also raised concerns among good government watchdogs, who have criticised Trump Media since the beginning of Trump's second term over the possibility of the company providing him a way to profit from the presidency. Democrats have said they would investigate the paid service if they gain control of Congress in the midterms.McGurn dismissed those concerns, pointing to the wider use of similar services.“Providing licensed real-time public data through commercial APIs is a well-established business practice across the technology, financial information and media industries,” he said. “This is no different.”Trump Media is not abandoning all of its new ventures. Its previously announced nuclear fusion business will continue, with McGurn saying the company hopes to complete its merger with energy company TAE Technologies by the end of the year.“We continue to believe it’s the single most important driver of long-term value for this company,” McGurn said of the fusion business.The company has $1 billion in debt through special convertible notes that are not due until 2028. However, lenders have an option to demand that the notes be cashed out in November, potentially affecting the company's finances, although it appeared to have ample cash at the end of the quarter.
Article Summary: Trump Media & Technology reported a $238 million loss in the second quarter. The three-month loss through June was more than 10 times the loss recorded a year earlier. The company also said it was changing course after a year of expanding into businesses beyond media.

Article Title: Catering cart & military aircraft: How Trump secretly moved out of Turkey amid Iran assassination threat
Article Text:
President Donald Trump speaks while switching planes at US Air Force Base RAF Mildenhall in Suffolk Eastern England, on his way back to Washington from the NATO summit in Ankara, Turkey. (AP/PTI image)

US President Donald Trump was secretly moved in an airport catering truck to a smaller military aircraft after boarding Air Force One in Ankara, a covert operation triggered by an Iranian assassination threat, The Washington Post reported Monday.Trump had initially boarded the older, baby-blue Air Force One in front of cameras after attending the Nato summit in Turkey.But after getting on the aircraft, he was secretly shuttled by an airport catering truck to an Air Force C-32A, which then flew him to Britain, the Post reported, citing a US official familiar with the operation and corroborating material it reviewed.The extraordinary security operation came as hostilities with Iran were escalating. Iran borders Turkey, where Trump had travelled for the Nato summit and made his first international trip aboard a newly renovated jet donated by Qatar.The president's unexpected switch from the new aircraft to the older Air Force One before leaving Ankara had raised questions over the security of the Qatari-donated plane.Trump had said on Truth Social before departing Ankara that he would use the older baby-blue Air Force One "for old time's sake" to fly to RAF Mildenhall in Britain, while the new aircraft would also stop at the same base so US service members stationed there could tour it.However, after Trump boarded the older aircraft in front of cameras, he was secretly transferred to the C-32A using an airport catering truck, according to the Post.The deception operation was triggered by a credible threat to Trump, the Post reported. A similar operation took place in 2000, when President Bill Clinton used an unmarked executive jet to fly into Pakistan while sending his formal Air Force One as a decoy.Also read: 'Blood for blood': Iran displays giant billboard with Donald, Melania and Trump children in coffins On this occasion, journalists who believed they were travelling with Trump aboard the older Air Force One were advised to keep their window shades in the press cabin closed. The Post reported that some White House staff also believed the president was on board.When reporters later asked Trump why they had been told to keep the shades shut during the flight, he said they were "probably on a dangerous flight." He went onto say: “But if I go, you go. Right?"The C-32A carrying Trump arrived in Britain at around 10:20 p.m., with the older Air Force One and media arriving minutes later, the Post reported. It was not immediately clear how Trump was transferred from the C-32A back to the older Air Force One.Trump's travelling press pool reported that he climbed down the stairs of the older Air Force One at 10:56 p.m. local time. He gave reporters a peace sign but did not walk over to speak with them.He then spent some time greeting US service members before walking towards the new Qatar-donated aircraft.Asked about the revelation that Trump had secretly travelled on a third aircraft, the White House provided a statement from Communications Director Steve Cheung saying the Qatari-donated jet had been fitted with high-level security protocols to protect the president and his staff."As the President has said recently, there are many enemies of America who have their sights on him, and we use every tool at our disposal to address those threats," Cheung said.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump was secretly moved in an airport catering truck to a smaller military aircraft after boarding Air Force One in Ankara. The Washington Post reported that the operation was triggered by an Iranian assassination threat. The extraordinary security operation came as hostilities with Iran were escalating. Iran borders Turkey, where Trump had travelled for the Nato summit.

Article Title: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman raises Hasina extradition with Indian envoy
Article Text:
Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman (L) with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka Monday

DHAKA: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman Monday raised the issue of the extradition of exiled Awami League leader and ex-PM Sheikh Hasina with Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi, emphasising that Dhaka was hopeful of a positive response, while cautioning India against "actions" that could hurt bilateral ties.Briefing reporters, foreign minister Khalilur Rahman, who was present at the "courtesy meeting", said Bangladesh wants all countries to respect the entire structure of the State, adding that "I believe India has understood Bangladesh's concerns". PM Tarique's advice that India should avoid actions that can hit ties was being seen as referring to Hasina's defiant virtual news conference last week in Delhi. "What Hasina did on Aug 5 was. ..she showed disrespect to the judiciary, one of the pillars of the State... and the Indian govt allowed that (news conference) to happen," said Khalilur."My impression, after speaking with them, is that they have understood it. We hope they will not do anything to undermine any pillar of our State again. This is our expectation, and based on my conversations with them, I am somewhat reassured that this incident will not be repeated," he further said of the Aug 5 presser by Hasina.In a statement, Bangladesh PM's office said the meeting between Tarique and Trivedi also "covered a range of important bilateral issues". The Indian high commission in Dhaka said Trivedi conveyed greetings from PM Narendra Modi and "the intent to work together with govt and people of Bangladesh in a positive, constructive and forward-looking manner."Bangladesh has also urged "India to hand over the suspected killers of Osman Hadi as early as possible", said Khalilur. In March, West Bengal Police arrested two Bangladeshis accused of his murder in the Indian town of Bongaon.Meanwhile, RAW chief Parag Jain arrived in Dhaka Sunday, reportedly as part of efforts to normalise ties between the two countries.
Article Summary: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman meets Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi in Dhaka. Rahman raises issue of extradition of exiled Awami League leader and ex- PM Sheikh Hasina. Foreign minister Khalilur Rahman: Bangladesh wants all countries to respect the entire structure of the State.

Article Title: As AI grips world, thrill of collecting vintage, iconic computers growing
Article Text:
Attendees play on Apple Macintosh computers from the 1980s at the Vintage Computer Festival in Mountain View, California

MOUNTAIN VIEW: Software engineer Josh Dersch loves old computers. He spends countless hours tinkering in his garage, trying to coax decades-old machines back to life. He estimates he owns more than 200 vintage computers and devices in his Seattle home. "It's always been fascinating to me to see the origins of things," Dersch said. "It's a fun challenge to debug and repair. You can understand the entire system from top to bottom."Dersch is part of a growing community of vintage computer collectors who are preserving the classic machines that helped launch the digital revolution. While Silicon Valley has since moved on to shaping the future of artificial intelligence, these hardware enthusiasts are intent on saving the Atari, Commodore and IBM machines that are ancestors to today's laptops, wearable devices and smart phones.Where others see junk, people like Dersch see artifacts of computer history that are worthy of attention and respect. They delight in hearing the beeps and chimes of their childhood and firing up a low-def game of "Pong" or "Space Invaders". "The enthusiasm for the history of computers and all the stuff around it is growing," said Erik Klein, president of the Vintage Computer Federation, which organises an annual festival at the Computer History Museum in Mountain View in the heart of Silicon Valley.This year, more than 3,500 people attended the two-day Vintage Computer Festival earlier this month that celebrated the 50th anniversary of Apple, founded in 1976 in nearby Cupertino, Calif. It featured a panel with co-founders Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne reminiscing about the company's early days as a scrappy startup led by the late Steve Jobs.Over a dozen such gatherings have since sprung up in cities across North America, South America and Europe. Growing interest is reflected in more demand for vintage computers in online marketplaces, Klein said. Iconic computers like the Apple-1 - the company's first product - can fetch hundreds of thousands of dollars.Klein, a Silicon Valley software engineering manager, was a passionate collector until his hobby overwhelmed his home and family life. He had as many as 150 computer systems crammed into his closets and garage. He said his beloved collection had become an "albatross" and he worried about burdening his family. So he started selling and giving away his machines until he only had a few favourites left at home.Now Klein channels his passion for vintage computers into organizing festivals, repair workshops, swap meets and other events as president of the Vintage Computer Federation. "So it's really about evangelising that history and evangelising this hobby of maintaining, collecting and enjoying this vintage technology," Klein said.
Article Summary: Software engineer Josh Dersch is part of a growing community of vintage computer collectors who are preserving the classic machines that helped launch the digital revolution. Over a dozen such gatherings have since sprung up in cities across North America, South America and Europe. This year, more than 3,500 people attended the two-day Vintage Computer Festival earlier this month.

Article Title: More than 1,75,000 visas revoked so far in Trump's second term: Majority due to criminal activities, DUI
Article Text:
When the State Department revokes the legal status of migrants and deems them illegal, it is called visa revocation.

What is visa revocation ?

A foreign national who was charged with felony rape and sexual battery – including of a victim who was mentally disabled.

A foreign national charged with felony kidnapping, human trafficking, and sexual exploitation of a minor.

A foreign national arrested for disorderly conduct, resisting arrest with violence, drunk driving, and domestic violence.

A US embassy in North Africa revoked over 100 visas for “birth tourist” parents who came to the United States primarily to give birth so their children would get US citizenship.

A foreign national charged with sodomy of a child and aggravated sexual battery.

A foreign national charged with over a dozen counts of possessing child sexual abuse material.

A foreign national was arrested for driving with heroin and a blood alcohol level more than 3x the legal limit.

Multiple foreign nationals who celebrated the assassination of Charlie Kirk, including one who stated “when fascists die, democrats don’t complain” and another who said he “died too late.”

A foreign national who claimed to operate a legitimate business helping vulnerable patients access healthcare helped orchestrate a massive Medicaid scam – billing for over $5 million of fake services.

A foreign national built a company on lies – faking revenue and fooling investors to swindle millions of dollars from clients. The foreign national used the false claims and forged letters to fraudulently secure a visa.

A foreign national who came to the US to teach young students and was then arrested for sexually assaulting one.

From classrooms to careers, Trump tightens the immigration squeeze

The US State Department Monday published the exact number of visas revoked in the second term of Donald Trump's presidency. As per the data, US has revoked more than 1,75,000 visas from foreign nationals who violated the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against US citizens, defrauded Americans, abused our immigration system, or endangered national security, the department said."The majority of these visas were revoked due to law enforcement encounters for a range of criminal activity, with assault, driving under the influence, theft, and drug crimes being the leading causes. A significant share of visas were revoked for reckless driving, sexual assault, child abuse, fraud and embezzlement, and other crimes," the department said.When the State Department revokes the legal status of migrants and deems them illegal, it is called visa revocation. It is different from denaturalization as denaturalization happens only to those who have become US citizens.Secretary of State Marco Rubio has determined that numerous foreign nationals are deportable on foreign policy grounds, including a Cuban national connected to a Cuban communist regime influence operation, Iranian nationals with connections to the Iranian regime, a Laotian child sex offender pardoned by Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, and a Kuwaiti national who wished for violence against the President of the United States and called Americans his “enemy", the department said giving a list of other significant visa revocations."Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio’s leadership, the State Department will continue to identify, investigate, and revoke the visas of foreign nationals who threaten the safety of the American people. A US visa is a privilege, not a right. The Department remains committed to using every tool available to protect our communities from those who abuse it," the department said.Also read: Visa revocation, travel ban for reckless drivers: US says no second chance to those who put American lives at risk The Trump administration is tightening the immigration rules facing foreign talent at both ends of the pipeline, from international students to highly skilled workers. A new DHS rule will replace the current ‘duration of status’ system for F-1 students with fixed periods of stay, generally capped at four years, while cutting the post-study grace period from 60 days to 30.The rules also restrict students’ ability to change programmes or fields of study, particularly at graduate level, potentially adding costs, delays and uncertainty. At the other end, the administration is considering scrapping the 60-day grace period for H-1B workers who lose their jobs. For Indians, who make up the largest group of international students in the US and a major share of H-1B workers, the changes could make studying, working and building a long-term life in America significantly more difficult.
Article Summary: The US State Department Monday published the exact number of visas revoked in the second term of Donald Trump's presidency. US has revoked more than 1,75,000 visas from foreign nationals who violated the terms of their visas, committed crimes, called for violence against US citizens, defrauded Americans.

Article Title: Italy’s Andrea Doria sank in 1956, but divers still explore its dangerous wreck despite 18 deaths
Article Text:
Representative Image of the Andrea Doria liner partially submerged amid fog and ocean currents (AI-generated image)

How the Andrea Doria sank after colliding with the Stockholm in 1956

Why divers call it the Mount Everest of wreck diving

How mixed gas diving changed what was possible at the wreck

What divers recovered from the wreck in 2025

Why salvage from the wreck remains a contested question

Seventy years after the Andrea Doria sank in the North Atlantic, divers are still descending to the deteriorating Italian liner, exploring newly exposed sections and recovering artefacts before parts of the wreck disappear for good. Eighteen divers have died while trying to explore it. The ship lies on its starboard side about 50 miles south of Nantucket, with the seabed roughly 250 feet below the surface, well beyond normal recreational diving depths. Powerful currents, limited visibility, cold water and long decompression stops make the descent demanding, while collapsing passages, loose metal and heavy silt add to the danger inside the ship itself. Decades on the seafloor have already reshaped the wreck, with whole decks collapsed and the vessel now standing about 30 feet shorter than it once did.The Andrea Doria left Genoa on July 17, 1956, carrying 1,706 passengers and crew, bound for New York on what would become its 101st and final transatlantic crossing. On July 25, nearing the end of that voyage, the ship ran into dense fog while the outbound liner Stockholm sailed in clearer conditions nearby, and officers on both vessels reached different conclusions about how to pass each other after tracking one another by radar.At 11.05 pm, the Andrea Doria's captain ordered a four-degree turn to port, and two minutes later the Stockholm's third officer ordered a roughly 22-degree turn to starboard. By the time the two ships spotted each other's lights at 11.10 pm, less than a mile separated them, and neither manoeuvre could prevent what followed. Less than a minute later, the Stockholm's reinforced bow struck the Andrea Doria's starboard side at 18.5 knots, driving about 40 feet into the larger ship and tearing open seven of its 11 decks just behind the bridge. The collision killed 46 people aboard the Andrea Doria and five aboard the Stockholm, though the liner stayed afloat for nearly 11 hours, long enough for nearby ships to rescue the remaining passengers before it finally sank the next morning.Divers reached the wreck almost immediately, with two men descending to it the very next day using wetsuits, basic equipment and an underwater camera, and expeditions have continued ever since. The site earned its nickname among divers because of both the difficulty of the descent and the dangers of entering the wreck itself, and eight divers died there between 1992 and 1999 alone. Rising about 80 feet from the seabed, the ship exposes divers to roughly six to eight times the pressure found at the surface, and they burn through their air supply at a similarly increased rate, raising the risk of narcosis, oxygen toxicity and decompression sickness. Inside the hull, divers must navigate sideways stairways, collapsing passages, decaying metal and dangling wires, and any silt disturbed along the way can billow into the water and sharply cut visibility within seconds.In 1996, divers Steve Gatto and Tom Packer became the first to reach the ship's engine room, and while filming its gauge panel, Gatto lost track of his exit route and began experiencing narcosis before finding his way back out using one of the strobe lights the pair had placed along their path. Mixed gas diving later allowed divers to replace some of the nitrogen in their tanks with helium, reducing narcosis and making deeper dives more manageable, though the technique brought its own complications, since divers still needed lengthy decompression stops and had to carry the correct gas mixture for each depth or risk a fatal mistake. Gatto, who has made more than 250 dives to the Andrea Doria over the years, has said some divers were substituting technology for the experience needed to dive safely.On July 11, 2025, diver Chris Ogden was around 230 feet below the surface inside a confined section of the wreck when he spotted the circular top of a gyrocompass repeater, a five-foot-tall brass navigation instrument that once stood on the ship's bridge wing. With only four dives left on the expedition and barely 40 minutes on the bottom each time, Ogden and his diving partner Joe Mazraani spent most of three dives clearing nets, cables and roughly eight feet of debris before finally freeing the instrument and lifting it to the surface using an inflatable bag rated for 500 pounds. The gyrocompass reached the surface largely intact, though its face was missing, and weeks later filmmaker Al Giddings came forward saying he had recovered that same piece decades earlier during a 1968 expedition and still had it in his home.Atlantic Wreck Salvage, whose ongoing recovery work at the site is documented on its own record of the Andrea Doria's history and diving conditions, has made annual trips to the wreck since 2010 and restores what it recovers for public display. Removing artefacts from historic shipwrecks continues to divide opinion, with some arguing that objects should remain in place or be recovered only by trained archaeologists, while divers who work the Andrea Doria counter that its rapid deterioration means items left behind risk being crushed or buried for good as more of the structure collapses. The wreck sits within a stretch of ocean that the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Stellwagen Bank National Marine Sanctuary recognises as part of the region's protected maritime heritage, underlining how significant these sites remain even as they continue to change. Seven decades after it went down, the Andrea Doria keeps exposing new sections of itself to the divers willing to reach it, even as more of the ship settles permanently into the seabed.
Article Summary: Andrea Doria sank after colliding with the Stockholm in 1956. Ship lies on its starboard side about 50 miles south of Nantucket, with the seabed roughly 250 feet below the surface. Decades on the seafloor have reshaped the wreck, with whole decks collapsed and the vessel now standing about 30 feet shorter than it once did.

Article Title: PhD student Vikram Mubayi found dead in lake after going missing on solo hiking trip in US
Article Text:
UC Santa Barbara PhD student Vikram Mubayi was found dead after going missing during a solo hike in California's Inyo National Forest.

Vikram Mubayi, a chemical engineering PhD student at the University of California, Santa Barbara (UCSB), was found dead on August 3 in California's Inyo National Forest, two days after he went missing during a solo hiking trip in the Big Pine Lakes area.According to local reports, Mubayi last contacted his family on the evening of August 1 before a search operation was launched by Inyo County Search & Rescue.Authorities later recovered Mubayi's body from Big Pine Lakes, and officials said the circumstances surrounding his death remain under investigation, with no indication of foul play.Born and raised in Hong Kong, Mubayi was described by his family as an experienced hiker.In a post on Reddit, his sibiling urged people to inform if someone had seen Vikram. "My brother Vikram is 6’3, 170lbs, dark hair, and has been out of contact since 8.30pm yesterday in the big pine lakes area in the eastern sierra, specifically around agassiz col. Have attached a link to his route here strava.com/routes/3516945857263630584. Did anyone happen to see him along the way? he last sent an update 8.37PM PST from the following coordinates: 37.10942° N, 118.52428° W" the post said."He’s a fairly experienced hiker and we think that he reached a reasonably easy part of the route, so would have expected him back by now. his car is still at the trailhead. So sorry if this is not the right place to post. can post somewhere else if there’s a better place," it added.The official confirmation is yet to come from the authorities.
Article Summary: Vikram Mubayi, a chemical engineering PhD student at the University of California, Santa Barbara, was found dead on August 3 in California's Inyo National Forest. The circumstances surrounding his death remain under investigation, with no indication of foul play.

Article Title: 7.4-magnitude Colombia earthquake: At least 77 killed, buildings collapse; toll 'could top 1,000'
Article Text:
Residents and rescue workers search through the rubble of a collapsed building

Governor of Chocó gives update on earthquake

A powerful earthquake struck western Colombia on Monday, leaving several people dead and causing widespread damage, with buildings collapsing and residents trapped in several cities. The tremor was felt across Colombia, including the capital Bogota, as well as in neighbouring Venezuela and Ecuador.At least 77 have been killed with toll expected to rise with some estimates saying it could rise cross 1,000. Risaralda province reported the highest toll, with 42 deaths, according to Governor Juan Diego Patino. In Pereira, buildings suffered major damage, while three people were killed in Manizales and one person died in Buenaventura after a building collapsed. In Cali, more than two dozen structures collapsed, with several people still trapped in the rubble, as reported by Reuters.The quake also disrupted air travel, with flights suspended at airports in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura as authorities inspected the facilities for structural issues after damage was reported.The US Geological Survey (USGS) and Colombia's geological service recorded the earthquake at magnitude 7.4.Its epicentre was near San Jose del Palmar in Choco province, at a depth of around 107 km (66 miles). The USGS warned that “Significant casualties and damage are likely and the disaster is potentially widespread.”Read more: Buildings collapse, panic grips residents as quake shakes Colombia - 10 visuals that capture horror Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella said in a post on X that he will personally supervise recovery efforts and install an emergency center in San Jose del Palmar. "I have directly assumed leadership of the emergency response in San José del Palmar. I have ordered the establishment of a Unified Command Post to coordinate the attention to the damages and the affected individuals. I have requested from the director of the UNGRD a detailed report on the situation and the most urgent needs. I will also be personally in Pereira to accompany the affected people and verify the Government's response," he said (translated from Spanish)Choco Governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi said there were injuries and significant damage to buildings in the provincial capital, Quibdo, while authorities began assessing the impact. She also warned of possible aftershocks. "We have just experienced a major ​earthquake in the ⁠departmentof Choco. ‌We are concerned ​about ​aftershocks. Although the epicenter was ⁠near San Jose del Palmar, there ​are injuries and significant damage ​to buildings in the capital, Quibdo. We are already carrying out a damage assessment and will issue the first official ‌report shortly," governor Nubia Carolina Cordoba-Curi said on X.Additionally, the governor ​of neighboring ​Risaralda province, Juan Diego Patino, told local Blu ⁠Radio there was "serious damage to some buildings" in Pereira, the ​provincial capital. "What has just occurred is very ​severe. The images are truly shocking, with people injured and building facades collapsed," he said.Meanwhile, Bogota's mayor, Carlos Galan, said on X there was no major damage in the capital.Five platoons of rescue soldiers are being deployed to areas across Colombia that may require attention following the earthquake this morning, the Colombian Army said in a post on X. “With specialized search and rescue capabilities in collapsed structures, our soldiers have high-precision technological means and canine binomials trained for the specific search for people."“We keep our capacities available to respond in a timely manner and protect the lives of Colombians,” it added.More than 2 million people were exposed to very strong shaking during the earthquake in Colombia, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS). The shaking, rated 7 out of 10 on the USGS scale, could cause “considerable damage in poorly built structures” and slight to moderate damage to well-built buildings, reported CNN.Zarzal, Pereira and Armenia were among the most populated cities likely affected. USGS estimated the widespread damage could result in “significant casualties”, with roughly a one-in-three chance that fatalities could exceed 1,000.
Article Summary: At least 77 people have been killed in the earthquake in western Colombia. The US Geological Survey (USGS) recorded the earthquake at magnitude 7.4. Its epicentre was near San Jose del Palmar in Choco province, at a depth of around 107 km (66 miles)

Article Title: Over 1 million evacuated as Typhoon Dolphin hits eastern China; 1,400 Shanghai flights cancelled
Article Text:
China issues red alert as Typhoon Dolphin approaches. (Photo: ANI)

More than a million people were evacuated across eastern China, including Shanghai, after Typhoon Dolphin made landfall on Sunday, bringing transport services across the region to a halt and raising fears of flooding and landslides.Dolphin first struck Yuhuan in Zhejiang province at 5.30pm local time, with maximum wind speeds of 150kmph, meteorological authorities said. It made a second landfall in the city of Wenzhou about an hour later.The storm caused widespread travel disruption, with 1,400 flights cancelled in Shanghai alone.Chinese authorities had earlier issued their highest-level red alert for Dolphin. According to the BBC, the typhoon had been downgraded to a tropical storm by Monday morning.Despite the downgrade, the system continued to move inland, with authorities warning of torrential rain, severe flooding and landslides through Wednesday.Heavy rain was forecast on Monday across Shandong, Henan, Hubei, Anhui, Jiangsu and Zhejiang provinces, as well as Shanghai.Local governments urged people to avoid outdoor activities as a precaution. Several major tourist attractions remained closed, including parts of Disneyland and Legoland, along with a number of viewing platforms on Shanghai's Bund waterfront.
Article Summary: Dolphin first struck Yuhuan in Zhejiang province at 5.30pm local time, with maximum wind speeds of 150kmph. It made a second landfall in the city of Wenzhou about an hour later. 1,400 flights cancelled in Shanghai alone.

Article Title: Tokyo's geisha population fell from about 13,000 in 1940 to around 200 today; one 86-year-old geisha is turning to AI and holograms to keep the culture alive
Article Text:
Years of hospitality

Worrying for the future

In one of the busy malls in Tokyo, Ikuko, Japan's oldest and most famous geisha dances for shoppers in an elegant black kimono with precise movements. Only, the 86-year-old isn't really there; it's her hologram, a 3D projection of her, displayed in a life-size white box. "Thank you very much," she said to passers-by, before bowing and changing to a younger version of herself, created with AI.While she doesn't think AI is "cut out for this dance" just yet, or to replace their legendary hospitality, with the geisha numbers dwindling in the country, Ikuko has resigned to embracing new things in order to save the country's most iconic art forms.Once, there were 200 geisha in Akasaka, the area of Tokyo where Ikuko practises. But over the years, she has watched their number fall to about 20. "I felt we had to preserve this culture, so I did it for the sake of that very culture," she told ABC News. "This is the era we are entering, so I have to go along with it."After an illustrious career, which includes being the first geisha awarded Japan's prestigious Order of the Rising Sun, Ikuko feels the responsibility to preserve the tradition. "I'm already at the end of my life," she said."My greatest regret is that I hope Tokyo's geisha districts will truly survive for another few decades."A Geisha is a traditional Japanese female entertainer. Gei means art and sha means person, literally translating to "person of art." They are professional artists skilled in traditional Japanese music, dance, singing and conversation. They live and work in special districts called hanamachi or flower towns. There were once dozens of them in the city, but today only six major hanamachi remain, while the number of geisha across the city has also fallen from about 13,000 in 1940 to around 200.With their striking white makeup and bold black wigs, geisha have been synonymous with Japan for centuries, but a lot of people, even locals, fail to understand what they do. Geisha operate largely behind closed doors, traditionally catering to an exclusive group of customers. They are artisans who are said to embody omotenashi, the Japanese art of wholehearted, selfless hospitality.They dedicate their lives to perfecting traditional Japanese arts, which they rehearse by day. At night, they host banquets in exclusive, high-end restaurants and specialist teahouses, which have traditionally been run on a referral-only basis, where new patrons must have an introduction from an existing client. At a banquet, they dance, play music on traditional instruments like the shamisen and taiko drum, and ensure conversation flows between guests."This is the very pinnacle of hospitality," Ikuko said. "Indeed, perhaps only the most distinguished guests are permitted to enter." In her career, she has entertained politicians, business leaders and chairmen.But she has also been confronted with the misconception that geisha are prostitutes. Once, during a visit to America, she ended up in hospital and had to spend her convalescence educating the nurses, who mistakenly thought she was a sex worker. Though having sex with clients has never been the job of a geisha, the lines have blurred at times, and Ikuko doesn't shy away from that history."In the old days, there were certainly many geisha who sacrificed themselves for their families and their households," she said. "Nobody wants that sort of thing anymore. There are no sellers and no buyers."It was in 1964, when Ikuko made her debut as a geisha in Tokyo as the city was hosting the Olympics. In the "busy, old days," she said, "if a booking for this banquet was 30 minutes, I'd have to rush straight off to the next one."But soon things began going downhill for the geisha. Iwashita Hisafumi, who was working in a prominent geisha district at the time, also remembers those days. It was 1993, and in an effort to clean up politics and protect confidentiality, then-prime minister Hosokawa Morihiro announced politicians and businessmen should stop using the restaurants, called ryotei, for meetings."From the very next day, I saw for myself that the customers stopped coming," Mr Iwashita said. "That was when the decline began." Ryotei restaurants started closing, and many of the city's geisha districts ceased to exist.Now a writer and expert on geisha, he is concerned Tokyo's remaining ryotei have been too slow to find new customers and income sources to keep the tradition alive. "Ultimately, it is culture, but culture cannot flourish where money doesn't flow," he said.Evolving with the new nowAt this point, everyone is trying to adapt to the ever-changing world. Geisha are no longer relying on referral or invitation to attend, and are instead advertising heavily on social media and taking bookings online. The experience has been tailored for tourists, with the crowd made up of guests from Mexico, Australia, the United States, Singapore and Germany."I feel we have to take one step, then another, and keep moving forward," said Okami Chikage, who became an apprentice geisha at just 15 years old and after 35 years of practising, took on a new role as the owner of Asakusa Miyakadori. "To do that, I think it might sometimes mean stepping slightly outside the tradition rather than sticking to it rigidly."Three geisha performed for the guests at the banquet, dancing and playing the shamisen, before playing a traditional drinking game called konpira fune fune.Geisha can have children in some areas, and technically they can get married and continue to practise, but many choose to retire to have a family. It's a life of intense dedication, but there are still young women signing up for it. These days, some geisha houses recruit apprentices online or on social media. Young hopefuls attend meetings with the houses to try to get accepted, and then it can take them anywhere from six months to several years to graduate.Ikuko wants the profession and legacy to continue and is lobbying for all six of Tokyo's major districts to come together for a joint performance. She believes promotion is key to preserving the tradition, and worries too few Japanese people even know there are still geisha in Tokyo.But first, she needs to persuade the city's politicians. She's currently meeting with a member of parliament and wants the Tokyo Metropolitan Government to protect the geisha districts.If the city government could help secure a venue for a joint performance, she believes the event could "bring the geisha world back to life, just like in the old days." In the meantime, she and her geisha recently took to the stage at the outdoor festival in her local neighbourhood of Akasaka, where they were greeted with loud cheers.
Article Summary: Ikuko, Japan's oldest and most famous geisha dances for shoppers in a mall. She is a hologram, a 3D projection of her, displayed in a life-size white box. Once, there were 200 geisha in Akasaka, the area of Tokyo where Ikuko practises. But over the years, she has watched their number fall to about 20.

Article Title: ‘We’re reducing them’: Trump targets childhood vaccine schedule, pushes separate MMR jabs
Article Text:
The order calls for childhood immunisations to be given at separate medical visits “to the maximum extent feasible”

Trump calls for fewer vaccines, separate appointments

Doctors warn of vaccination gaps

US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order seeking sweeping changes to the country’s childhood vaccination recommendations, including reducing the number of vaccines routinely recommended for children and separating combination shots into multiple appointments.The order calls for childhood immunisations to be given at separate medical visits “to the maximum extent feasible” and directs the US government to work towards making individual measles, mumps and rubella vaccines available. The move revives Trump’s long-standing claims about vaccine safety and autism, despite decades of research finding no evidence of a link between childhood vaccines and autism.The changes have drawn strong criticism from doctors and public health experts, who warn that spacing out vaccinations could leave children vulnerable to preventable diseases and make it harder for families to complete recommended immunisation schedules.Speaking at the signing ceremony, Trump said his administration was adopting “gold standard” recommendations covering 11 core diseases, down from 18 diseases covered by recommendations at the end of 2024.The vaccines continuing to have full recommendations cover measles, mumps, rubella, diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, polio, Haemophilus influenzae type B, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus and chickenpox.“We're reducing them,” Trump said. “It's not only that you're doing fewer vaccines, or jabs, as they say, but you're doing them in a series of visits to the doctor.”The order also seeks to split the combined MMR vaccine into three separate shots once individual vaccines become available in the US. Trump suggested the combined vaccine could be dangerous.“Together, there could be a possibility they’re quite lethal,” Trump said of the MMR vaccine at the signing of the order on Monday.However, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says there is “no published scientific evidence that shows any benefit in separating the combination MMR vaccine into three individual shots”. It also says getting the MMR vaccine is safer than contracting measles, mumps or rubella.Public health experts have raised concerns that requiring multiple appointments could increase the chances of children contracting vaccine-preventable diseases before receiving their next dose. Families could also be more likely to miss appointments when vaccinations are spread across several visits.Dr Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics, criticised the changes, saying they would create unnecessary uncertainty.“Science about vaccines and their efficacy has not changed,” he said. “The distribution of viruses and other pathogens in our environment has not changed. Children in this country have not changed in the last 48 hours."Republican Senator Bill Cassidy, a doctor and chair of the Senate health committee, also opposed the order.“I'm a doctor. This executive order is wrong,” the Louisiana senator wrote. “The President does not have the expertise to make these changes.”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order seeking sweeping changes to the country’s childhood vaccination recommendations. The order calls for childhood immunisations to be given at separate medical visits “to the maximum extent feasible” and directs the US government to work towards making individual measles, mumps and rubella vaccines available. Doctors and public health experts warn that spacing out vaccinations could leave children vulnerable to preventable diseases.

Article Title: US records hottest month ever as July heat shatters 132-year-old record
Article Text:
The record came after weeks of intense heatwaves, prolonged periods of extreme temperatures and widespread wildfires.

Heat domes push temperatures to record levels

Heat takes toll on daily life

The United States has recorded its hottest month in more than a century of official temperature records. July’s average temperature was 76.89F (24.94C) across the Lower 48 states, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The Lower 48 refers to all US states except Alaska and Hawaii.The average was 3.3F (1.8C) above the 20th-century average and narrowly surpassed the previous record set in July 1936, when severe drought and extreme heat devastated large parts of the country.The record came after weeks of intense heatwaves, prolonged periods of extreme temperatures and widespread wildfires. Scientists say the severity of the heat is consistent with the effects of human-driven climate change, which is making extreme heat more frequent, longer-lasting and more intense.Three major heat dome events developed across the US during July, trapping hot air over large areas beneath slow-moving high-pressure systems. Extreme heat affected the West, Rockies, Upper Midwest, Gulf Coast and Southeast, with temperatures remaining well above normal for prolonged periods.Every state in the Lower 48 recorded a July average at least 1F (0.6C) above its 20th-century average, NOAA said.Wyoming experienced its hottest July on record, as well as its hottest month ever recorded, with average temperatures 5.1F above normal.The biggest factor behind the national record was unusually warm nights. The average minimum temperature across the Lower 48 exceeded the previous record by 0.7F. Scientists say rising overnight temperatures are particularly dangerous because they prevent the human body from recovering from daytime heat.“If you’re talking heat waves, that nighttime low is incredibly important for determining total heat stress,” said Jeff Masters, a meteorologist with Yale Climate Connections. “So if it doesn’t cool off at night, your body doesn’t have time to readjust to all the heat.”The heat was accompanied by widespread wildfires in the Pacific Northwest and Canada, with smoke affecting large parts of North America. Scientists have linked the growing frequency and intensity of extreme heat and wildfire conditions to the continued burning of coal, oil and gas.The extreme conditions also affected Americans’ everyday lives. An AP-NORC poll found that nearly half of respondents said higher electricity bills caused by increased air-conditioning use had a major impact on their finances. Around 40% said extreme heat had disrupted their travel plans, while about two-thirds reported changes to family outdoor activities.Around half said the heat had affected their exercise routines, with the overall impact broader than when similar questions were asked two years earlier.Masters said surpassing a temperature record from the Dust Bowl era was particularly concerning given the historic devastation caused by the drought and heat of the 1930s.
Article Summary: July’s average temperature was 76.89F (24.94C) across the Lower 48 states. The average was 3.3F (1.8C) above the 20th-century average. The record came after weeks of intense heatwaves, prolonged periods of extreme temperatures and widespread wildfires.

Article Title: ‘Bones poking out, blood everywhere’: 10-foot alligator attacks Florida paddleboarder and tears off her arm; quick-thinking boater rushes to save her
Article Text:
​Florida woman loses arm after 10-foot alligator drags her underwater in Silver River; quick-thinking boater rushes to save her

Alligator pulls woman underwater in Florida river

Boater scares alligator away and stops bleeding

Silver River temporarily closed after alligator attack

Recent alligator attacks in Florida

A Florida woman survived a terrifying alligator attack after a nearly 10-foot reptile grabbed her arm and pulled her underwater while she was paddleboarding in the Silver River. A quick-thinking boater rushed to help after hearing screams and managed to scare the alligator away before using a rope to control her severe bleeding.The woman was paddleboarding with her family in the Silver River in north-central Florida when the alligator suddenly attacked.According to FOX35, the reptile grabbed her arm and dragged her underwater. She reportedly tried to fight it off with her paddle, but the alligator continued its attack.John Gamache, who was eating lunch on his boat nearby, heard the victim’s family shouting for help and immediately headed towards them.“I looked just upriver from us a couple hundred feet and saw an alligator head way above the water and going full speed towards the swimmers,” Gamache told FOX35.Gamache said the sound and movement of his boat caused the alligator to retreat. However, the woman had suffered a devastating arm injury and was losing blood rapidly.“It was a terrible injury, bones poking out, blood everywhere. Obviously, the minutes mattered,” he said.Gamache used a rope from his boat to tie off the woman’s wound and help control the bleeding while his father focused on getting the other swimmers and children safely out of the water.First responders subsequently took the injured woman to a nearby hospital for treatment.Her family confirmed on Sunday that she had been discharged and was recovering at home. They also expressed their gratitude to Gamache for intervening so quickly.“They called earlier, and we talked for a while, and it was heartwarming to hear them explain their emotions,” Gamache said.“We’re glad that it happened as good as it could have. Like the result is just the sustained injury and nothing more,” he added.Following the attack, officials temporarily closed the Silver River while a trapper worked to remove the alligator from the water.Marion County officials said the reptile measured approximately 9 feet 8 inches. The river was reopened to the public on Sunday after the alligator was removed.Gamache, who has been visiting Silver Springs throughout his life, said he had never witnessed an alligator attack in the area before.The latest incident comes amid a series of serious alligator attacks in Florida and surrounding areas.Just weeks earlier, 31-year-old Brittany Clark was killed by a 12-foot alligator while she was paddling in the shallows of the Econlockhatchee River at Little Big Econ State Forest on June 28.Clark’s boyfriend made a desperate 911 call after the attack, pleading with emergency responders to reach the scene.Another serious incident occurred in Marion County on June 27, when 11-year-old Brodie Terry, from Pennsylvania, lost his hand after an approximately 8-foot-7-inch alligator bit him while he was fishing with his father.Terry was reportedly preparing to release a fish back into the water when the alligator clamped onto his hand.
Article Summary: The woman was paddleboarding with her family in the Silver River in north- central Florida when the alligator suddenly attacked. She reportedly tried to fight it off with her paddle, but the reptile continued its attack. A quick- thinking boater heard the victim's family shouting for help and immediately headed towards them. He used a rope to tie off the woman's wound and help control the bleeding.

Article Title: US judge dismisses criminal case against Gautam Adani
Article Text:
The US Justice Department announced on May 18 that it would no longer pursue the prosecution

A US judge on Monday dismissed criminal charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani after the Justice Department decided to abandon a long-running fraud and bribery case against him.Brooklyn-based US District Judge Nicholas Garaufis approved federal prosecutors’ request to dismiss the case after seeking further clarification on why they wanted to drop the charges. The judge had also asked Adani whether he was aware of any agreement involving a promise or benefit in exchange for the dismissal.Adani, chairman of the Adani Group , welcomed the court’s decision and said his faith in the legal process had remained firm throughout the case."I welcome the US court’s decision with humility and deep respect for the judicial process. Throughout this challenging period, our faith in truth, fairness and the rule of law remained unwavering. My deepest gratitude to those who never lost faith in us, in the system and in India’s capacity for justice. We will continue doing what matters: building for our nation, creating value that outlasts us and serving a purpose larger than ourselves. That is our commitment"The charges against Adani were filed in 2024. US prosecutors accused him of misleading American investors by providing assurances about the company’s anti-corruption practices.The Adani Group has consistently denied wrongdoing, while Adani himself had not appeared in a US court to respond to the allegations.The Justice Department announced on May 18 that it would no longer pursue the prosecution, saying the case was primarily foreign, difficult to prove and inconsistent with the agency’s current priorities.In a July 4 court filing, senior Justice Department official Trent McCotter also rejected reports that the decision was linked to Adani’s pledge to invest $10 billion in the United States. He said such reports were false.The judge had sought assurances after questioning the circumstances surrounding the dismissal. In response, Adani said in a sworn declaration filed on July 15 that he was not aware of any agreement exchanging anything for the dismissal of the indictment.
Article Summary: A US judge on Monday dismissed criminal charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani. The Justice Department decided to abandon a long-running fraud and bribery case against him. Adani, chairman of the Adani Group, welcomed the court’s decision.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael Jordan: "The game is my wife. It demands loyalty and responsibility, and it gives me…." - a powerful lesson in commitment, discipline and fulfilment
Article Text:
Michael Jordan (Image: Wikipedia)

Quote of the day by Michael Jordan

"The game is my wife. It demands loyalty and responsibility, and it gives me back fulfillment and peace"

What is the meaning behind the quote by Michael Jordan

A companion quote that goes even further

Why real commitment is essential for success

Why discipline can genuinely create freedom

Why meaningful work can genuinely provide fulfilment

Why loyalty matters through the difficult stretches

Why responsibility naturally follows real ambition

Why sacrifice is simply part of real achievement

Why this idea reaches well beyond basketball

Other famous quotes by Michael Jordan

"Talent wins games, but teamwork and intelligence win championships."

"I've failed over and over and over again in my life. And that is why I succeed."

"Some people want it to happen, some wish it would happen, others make it happen."

"Limits, like fears, are often just an illusion."

Why this quote is relevant today

Great achievements rarely happen by accident. Behind almost every extraordinary success sits a long stretch of discipline, sacrifice and genuine commitment. Michael Jordan captured exactly that relationship with basketball in a single striking comparison. "The game is my wife," he said. "It demands loyalty and responsibility, and it gives me back fulfillment and peace. " For Jordan, basketball was never simply a job or a route to fame. It asked for real dedication, and in return it gave him something worth just as much, a lesson he returned to repeatedly across a career defined by an unusually consistent, sustained level of commitment.Jordan is comparing basketball to a lifelong relationship. A genuine relationship demands loyalty, real attention and a sense of responsibility, and Jordan believed his own connection to the game asked for exactly the same things. He had to train consistently, keep real discipline, and accept the sacrifices that came with performing at the very highest level. In return, the game gave him something equally valuable, a genuine sense of fulfilment and peace. The quote is really suggesting that meaningful dedication was never only about what someone gives up.It is just as much about what that commitment gives back.Jordan expanded on this same idea elsewhere, describing basketball in even more personal terms. "The game of basketball has been everything to me," he said. "My place of refuge, place I've always gone where I needed comfort and peace. It's been the site of intense pain and the most intense feelings of joy and satisfaction. It's a relationship that has evolved over time, given me the greatest respect and love for the game. " Read alongside today's quote, it becomes clear this was never a passing comparison. It reflected something Jordan genuinely felt across his entire career.Talent can create a real opportunity, but commitment is what actually decides what someone does with it. Jordan became one of basketball's greatest players not purely through natural ability, but because he kept investing real time and effort into getting better, year after year. Consistent commitment is really what turns raw potential into actual performance.Discipline usually gets associated with restriction. In practice, disciplined habits tend to create more freedom rather than less. Someone who consistently prepares, practises and improves becomes considerably more capable of handling a real challenge when it actually arrives. The confidence that comes from that preparation lets a person perform without constantly second-guessing whether they are actually ready.Work often gets viewed purely as a way to earn a living. People can also find real identity, purpose and satisfaction through what they do, and Jordan's own relationship with basketball shows exactly how a meaningful pursuit can become a central part of someone's life. Once work genuinely aligns with real passion and purpose, effort starts to feel rewarding rather than simply demanding.Loyalty means staying committed even once things genuinely get difficult. Every worthwhile pursuit runs into real frustration, failure, setbacks and fatigue at some point. People who stay committed through those difficult stretches tend to be the ones who eventually experience the actual rewards that only come from sustained, long-term development.Wanting success is the easy part. Actually accepting the responsibility required to reach it is considerably harder. Jordan's quote ties loyalty directly to responsibility because genuine commitment always requires real action, taking ownership of your own preparation, your own decisions and your own performance.Extraordinary goals usually require giving up some genuinely ordinary comforts along the way. Time that could go toward relaxing sometimes has to go toward practising instead. Jordan's entire career is a demonstration of how sustained, repeated sacrifice can eventually produce genuinely extraordinary results.Jordan's underlying philosophy applies to almost any meaningful pursuit. A musician can treat their craft with exactly the same level of dedication. An entrepreneur can commit fully to building a company. A student can devote themselves to properly mastering a subject. The underlying principle stays the same everywhere it applies, meaningful achievement requires sustained, genuine commitment.Jordan's words are a reminder that success was never simply about possessing talent. It is about actually building a real relationship with the pursuit itself. Once something genuinely matters to a person, discipline becomes considerably easier to sustain, because the effort behind it actually carries real meaning. "The game is my wife. It demands loyalty and responsibility, and it gives me back fulfillment and peace" is really more than a quote about basketball. It teaches that meaningful pursuits demand consistency, responsibility and real sacrifice, but they can also give back something genuinely invaluable in return, a sense of purpose, satisfaction and lasting fulfilment.
Article Summary: "The game is my wife. It demands loyalty and responsibility, and it gives me back fulfillment and peace" Behind almost every extraordinary success sits a long stretch of discipline, sacrifice and genuine commitment. Jordan became one of basketball's greatest players not purely through natural ability, but because he kept investing real time and effort into getting better, year after year.

Article Title: Smash-and-grab jewelry heist at Indian store in New Jersey: Valuables worth $1 million stolen in 1 minute
Article Text:
Masked men looted jewelry worth $1 million from an Indian jewelry store, 9Lakha, in New Jersey.

Four masked men broke into an Indian jewelry store, 9Lakha, on Oak Tree Road in New Jersey and looted valuables worth $1 million in under 1 minute. Surveillance video showed an SUV stopped in front of the store and four masked men ran inside. They smashed the display cases with sledgehammers and put the jewelry in their bags. Sonu Chauhan, owner of the one-year-old store, told local channels that they were done within 30 to 45 seconds.“They had big plastic bags with them. Along with the trays, they would start dumping into those bags. Within 30 or 45 seconds, they were done. The car was there, and they got into it," Chauhan said.The incident took place on Saturday evening. Chauhan said the robbers took the entire inventory of the store.The store is located in an area dotted by Indian jewelry stores and hence an easy target by organized crime. Virani Jewellers on the same street was robbed with a similar tactic in June last year, and also in 2022.Co-owner of 9Lakha, Sushmita Chauhan, told News12 NJ: "It would be very beneficial to see if the government or the town can give a little bit of insurance to the street”. They should “put some preventative measures rather than just going and acting after something really bad happened”, she said.Similar such heists took place in other Indian jewelry stores too: Ruby's Jeweller in Perth Amboy was robbed in May last year, and Reema Jewellers in Jersey City earlier this year, and Popular London Jewel, also in Jersey City, last November.
Article Summary: Four masked men broke into an Indian jewelry store, 9Lakha, on Oak Tree Road in New Jersey and looted valuables worth $1 million. Surveillance video showed an SUV stopped in front of the store and four masked men ran inside. They smashed the display cases with sledgehammers and put the jewelry in their bags.

Article Title: AOC releases new video showing her egg freezing process as she does not rule out 2028 presidential run
Article Text:
Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez asks the Internet not to be weird about it as she takes an injection as part of her egg freezing process.

Who is AOC's partner Riley Roberts?

Democrat leader Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez announced that she opted to freeze her eggs as she decides her next political move, including the 2028 presidential election. “This is a choice that I am making to feel more in control of my life,” the 36-year-old Rep said on Instagram, adding that she was aware that she took a political risk in divulging these personal details on social media.She said later on ABC's “This Week” on Sunday that she has not ruled out running for president or for the US Senate seat held by Democrats’ floor leader, Chuck Schumer of New York, in 2028. She explained that she wants to normalize conversations about what women face in their professional and personal lives, while also highlighting the policies of President Donald Trump’s administration.The she posted more videos of the freezing process as she released a video of her unboxing the medicines and then taking an injection in the belly.“In this political environment, where this administration is denying reproductive care to women across the country, from abortion rights to the ability to carry out a healthy pregnancy, I think it’s important for us as leaders to have these conversations,” she said.AOC said she thought her fertility decision was 'bada**' and noted that men do not have to deal with it.Ocasio-Cortez revealed that her insurance did not cover the process and she paid everything on her own.She explained that there are two parts of the costs: one part is for the medicine and the second is for the process and the clinic. AOC said she saved for a long time for the expenditure and it would cost her around $8K-$9K.AOC got engaged to Riley Roberts in 2022 though their relationship has been long. They met as undergrads at Boston University. The couple started dating after becoming acquainted during a weekly debate event and remained together throughout their college careers, according to the biography Take Up Space: The Unprecedented AOC. While they ultimately broke up after graduation, they found their way back to each other several years later.Roberts is from Arizona and he works in the marketing and web development field.
Article Summary: Ocasio-Cortez revealed that her insurance did not cover the process and she paid everything on her own. AOC said she saved for a long time for the expenditure and it would cost her around $8K-$9K. She got engaged to Riley Roberts in 2022 though their relationship has been long.

Article Title: Lake Mead fell to 1,040.4 feet as the Colorado River crisis deepened; Lake Powell is also under pressure, raising questions over water and hydropower
Article Text:
A paddle boat in Lake Mead near the Hoover Dam, far below the bathtub ring of light minerals indicating the lack of water, near Boulder City, Nev., on Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Ty ONeil)

A record low across the Colorado River system

Hydropower would be affected first

Dead pool would threaten water deliveries

Arizona, California, and Mexico would face different risks

Las Vegas has an unusual advantage

A tourist takes a photo of Lake Mead near Boulder City, Nev., on Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (AP Photo/Ty ONeil)

Wildlife and tourism are also at risk

A crisis that would unfold in stages

(With inputs from AP)

Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in the United States, has reached its lowest recorded level since it was created nearly 90 years ago, according to AP News. The reservoir fell to 1,040.4 feet above sea level, just below its previous record low from July 2022. At the same time, Lake Powell, the country’s second-largest reservoir, remains dangerously depleted, raising concerns about the future of water supplies, hydropower, agriculture, wildlife, and communities across the Southwest.The two reservoirs are the backbone of the Colorado River system. Together, they help manage water for roughly 40 million people across seven U.S. states, Tribal communities, and Mexico. They also store water from wet years so cities and farms can continue receiving supplies during prolonged drought.But after years of low snowpack, extreme heat, drought, overuse, and rising evaporation, that reserve is rapidly shrinking. The question is no longer simply whether the lakes look low. It is what would happen if Lake Powell and Lake Mead fell so far that they could no longer perform their most important functions.Lake Mead is held back by Hoover Dam near Las Vegas, along the Arizona-Nevada border. Its recent decline reflects stress across the entire Colorado River Basin, particularly in the Rocky Mountains, where melting snow provides much of the river’s annual flow.The basin experienced its worst snowpack on record during the past winter, adding pressure to a river system already struggling with chronic drought and decades of demand exceeding natural supplies. Both Lake Mead and Lake Powell are now at levels not seen in nearly seven decades, while the combined storage of the two reservoirs has fallen to a historic low, according to CNN.The consequences are already visible. Boat ramps and marinas have had to close, move, or be rebuilt as shorelines retreat. At Lake Powell, visitors face increasingly difficult access to the water, while recreation-based businesses around both reservoirs are losing income.The crisis has also forced federal officials to make difficult choices. The Bureau of Reclamation recently proposed that Arizona, California, and Nevada, the three Lower Basin states, reduce their water use. However, the states have struggled to agree on how the cuts should be distributed over the long term, according to PBS.The first major operational warning would likely come from hydropower production.At Glen Canyon Dam, which holds back Lake Powell, electricity generation depends on the pressure created by the height of the water above the turbines. As the reservoir level falls, that pressure weakens. Lake Powell is about 23% full and has been reported to be only a few dozen feet above the elevation at which Glen Canyon Dam can no longer generate electricity, as per AP News.The dam has an installed generating capacity of approximately 1,320 megawatts. Its electricity is distributed across several Western states and supports municipalities, irrigation districts, rural cooperatives, government agencies, and Tribal communities.A shutdown would not automatically plunge the Southwest into darkness. The regional power grid includes natural gas, coal, nuclear, solar, wind, and other sources. But Glen Canyon Dam offers flexible power that can respond quickly to periods of high demand, such as hot summer afternoons, or when solar and wind generation drops.Replacing that power could lead to higher electricity prices and greater pressure on smaller utilities and irrigation districts. Revenue from federal hydropower also helps support dam maintenance, salinity-control programs, environmental projects, and other Colorado River initiatives. Losing those sales would therefore create financial consequences beyond the power grid.Hoover Dam would face a similar problem as Lake Mead falls. The dam can continue releasing water after its turbines stop operating, but its electricity production declines as the reservoir loses hydraulic pressure. The loss of hydropower at both dams would make an already strained Western energy system more expensive and less flexible.“Dead pool” does not mean a reservoir contains no water. It means the water surface has fallen below the lowest outlet that can release stored water downstream through the existing infrastructure.For Lake Powell, the minimum power pool is generally associated with an elevation near 3,490 feet. Hydropower can stop before the reservoir reaches its absolute dead-pool level, but water may still pass through lower outlet structures for a time. If the lake falls too far, however, releases would become increasingly difficult and less reliable.At that point, Lake Powell would no longer function as the Upper Basin’s drought reserve. The reservoir currently allows managers to store water during strong snowmelt years and release it gradually during dry periods. Without that buffer, downstream flows would depend much more directly on the amount of water arriving in a particular season.Some relief might come with a wet winter, but a bad snow year would be felt more quickly by communities and farms. Water timing is as important as total quantity. Crops need water for growing seasons. Cities need steady supplies. Downstream reservoirs need scheduled releases.Lake Mead is even more important for the Lower Basin. Hoover Dam’s intake structures allow water to move toward Arizona, California, and Mexico. If Lake Mead fell to approximately 895 feet, the reservoir would reach the dead-pool threshold for those existing intakes, meaning stored water could no longer pass through Hoover Dam in the normal way.Legal water rights would not solve that physical problem. A state, farm, city, or irrigation district may have a senior claim to Colorado River water, but that entitlement cannot move water through an intake that is no longer submerged.Arizona would likely experience some of the earliest and deepest reductions. Much of the Central Arizona Project has junior priority within the Lower Basin, and agricultural users have already absorbed significant cuts under existing shortage rules.If the river could no longer supply the Central Arizona Project, farms in central Arizona could face extensive fallowing. Some growers might turn to groundwater, but increased pumping would raise costs and worsen problems such as aquifer depletion, land subsidence, failing wells, and ground fissures.Phoenix and Tucson would not immediately run out of water. Both cities have groundwater, conservation programs, reclaimed water, storage reserves, and other sources. The Phoenix area also receives supplies from the Salt and Verde rivers. Still, a prolonged loss of Colorado River water would likely bring tighter outdoor-use restrictions, higher water costs, stricter development rules, and major investments in recycling and alternative supplies.California’s senior water rights would provide protection during ordinary shortages, particularly for agricultural districts such as those in the Imperial and Coachella valleys. But those rights would not guarantee deliveries if Hoover Dam could no longer release stored water.Southern California has a more varied water portfolio, including supplies from Northern California, local groundwater, reservoirs, conservation, recycling, and the Colorado River Aqueduct. That diversity could help cities manage a temporary disruption. The situation would become far more severe if Colorado River failure occurred alongside drought in the Sierra Nevada.Mexico would face a major treaty and humanitarian challenge. The 1944 Water Treaty generally provides Mexico with 1.5 million acre-feet of Colorado River water each year, although binational agreements allow reductions during shortages. If releases through the Lower Basin system stopped altogether, agriculture in Mexico’s Mexicali Valley and communities in Baja California would need to rely more heavily on groundwater, conservation, reuse, transfers, or emergency supplies.Southern Nevada has invested heavily in infrastructure designed to keep Las Vegas connected to Lake Mead as the lake declines. A deep-water intake and low-lake-level pumping station allow the Southern Nevada Water Authority to draw water from elevations below Hoover Dam’s ordinary intake threshold.That gives Las Vegas more time than many other communities. The city also recycles most indoor water: wastewater from showers, sinks, and toilets is treated and returned to Lake Mead. Outdoor irrigation, by contrast, consumes water through evaporation and plant growth.Even Las Vegas would not have unlimited protection. If the lake continued falling, pumping would become more difficult and expensive. The city’s ability to maintain supplies would depend on conservation and limiting water that is permanently consumed.The reservoirs’ decline would affect more than people and power systems. Lake Powell releases relatively cold water from deep within the reservoir, helping shape the temperature of the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon. As water levels fall and releases become warmer, invasive fish such as smallmouth bass may find more favorable conditions.That is a concern for native species, including the threatened humpback chub. Federal officials have already made decisions about how to manage cold water releases from Glen Canyon Dam while trying to protect both hydropower operations and native fish habitat.Recreation would suffer well before either reservoir reached dead pool. Boat ramps become unusable as shorelines retreat, and marinas and roads must be repeatedly relocated. Communities near Lake Mead and Lake Powell could lose income from boating, fishing, lodging, equipment rentals, and tourism.A simultaneous failure of Lake Powell and Lake Mead is not an overnight scenario, nor is it the current federal forecast.
